global.concept_prompt: PLACEHOLDER — finalize in the craftsmanship/storytelling pass. Photorealistic documentary footage at ONE fixed, recognizable watch-restoration workbench (the channel's signature setting, identical every episode). A single watchmaker's hands restore one vintage wristwatch from neglected/non-running condition to fully serviced and gleaming: teardown, cleaning, rust/grime removal, part repair, reassembly, regulation, case/crystal polish, final beauty shot. Locked, controlled macro lighting. Hand tools only. No faces, no text/logos baked into frames (all text is overlay-only).
global.style_notes: PLACEHOLDER. Photoreal macro bench documentary realism. Same workbench, mat, lighting, and tool layout every episode for brand recognition. Each clip is a distinct angle/zoom of a cleaning or repair step. Watch identity (dial, case, hands, movement) stays IDENTICAL across the whole video; only its condition (dirty → restored) changes.
rules: Exactly one person (the watchmaker); only the hands and forearms are visible — never a face.
The workbench, mat, lighting, and background are the same recognizable setting in every scene and every episode.
Hand tools and bench equipment only — no industrial machinery.
The watch's identity is locked: same dial, case, hands, and movement throughout; only its condition changes from neglected to restored.
No text, numbers, logos, or watermarks baked into any frame — all text comes from the overlay system.
Photorealistic; never cartoon, anime, or stylized.
global.negative_prompt: PLACEHOLDER. face, person's face, multiple hands, multiple people, text, watermark, logo, subtitles, cartoon, anime, CGI look, changing watch model mid-video, different workbench, morphing watch, warped geometry, extra fingers, blurry, low quality

planning.planner_system_prompt: You plan a satisfying watch-restoration video at a fixed macro workbench. Each scene is one clear restoration step shown from a distinct angle/zoom, progressing from a neglected watch to a fully restored one.
first_scene_hook_rules: Scene 1 opens on the signature empty workbench, then the watchmaker's hands place the neglected watch down — the 'before' state.
viral_pacing_rules: Each scene shows visible restoration progress — never repeat the same step.
Alternate macro detail shots with slightly wider bench shots.
The final scene is the satisfying restored-and-running reveal.
scene_progression_rules: Strict order: teardown → clean → de-rust/de-grime → repair → reassemble → polish/regulate → final reveal.
The watch must stay the same identity; only its condition advances.
start_state_rules: K0 = the signature empty workbench (the recurring brand setting), with the neglected watch about to be worked on. This is the 'before' anchor and the same setting every episode.
Show the watch in clearly neglected/non-running condition: dull, dirty, scratched, possibly stopped.

composition_rules: Macro framing on the watch and the watchmaker's hands at the fixed bench.
Keep the same lighting and background as the style bible's locked setting.
continuity_rules: Lock the watch's identity (dial, case, hands, movement) and the bench/lighting IDENTICALLY across all keyframes.
Vary only the camera angle, zoom, and the current restoration step — NOT the watch model or the setting.
Each keyframe is a self-contained composition (clips are clean cuts between angles, not morphs).

camera_rules: Locked, controlled bench camera; smooth, minimal movement.
ManCave-style POV is NOT used here.
motion_rules: Realistic close hand motion performing the restoration step.
The watch's identity must not morph or change; no teleporting parts.
motion.negative_prompt_extra: morphing watch, changing dial, changing case, extra fingers, warped tools, flicker, jitter, text, watermark, logo

items.content_prompt: Write a 1-line on-screen hook (<=9 words, ALL CAPS, no emojis/punctuation) tied to THIS episode's watch-owner story — heart-tugging or 'wow'. Use the provided Story summary. Example shapes: 'HER GRANDFATHER WORE THIS EVERY DAY' / 'FORGOTTEN IN A DRAWER FOR 40 YEARS'.

metadata.title_prompt: Write a curiosity/emotion-driven title (<=100 chars) for a vintage watch restoration short, reflecting THIS episode's owner story. No clickbait lies.
metadata.description_prompt: Write an engaging description (<=500 chars): the watch's story, the restoration, a light CTA.
metadata.hashtag_prompt: 8-12 hashtags mixing watch-restoration/horology niche tags with broad satisfying-restoration tags.

voiceover.script_prompt: PLACEHOLDER — refine in the storytelling pass. You are a master short-form storyteller. Write a narration that tells the TRUE-feeling story of THIS watch's owner: who they were, how the watch came to the bench, why it had to be saved, and the emotional payoff when it runs again. Open on a 2-second hook that promises heartbreak-or-wonder; one spoken idea per beat; build to the reveal; end on a line that earns a 'wow' or a tear. No 'today I'll show you'. Match the restoration steps on screen.

memory.instruction: Do not repeat the same watch type, owner story archetype, or restoration angle across recent episodes. Vary the watch (dress/diver/chronograph/military/pocket), the owner's story, and the standout restoration moment while keeping the locked bench setting.
